Description:

**Location**: Los Angeles, CA (50% travel)

**Position**: Full-Time

**Reports To**: Director of Customer Experience

TGR Solutions, Inc. designs and builds autonomous robots for regulated environments and is based in the heart of Los Angeles, California. TGR develops robotics solutions from the ground up and builds integrated systems that help organizations apply robotics and AI to demanding work.

TGR’s flagship product line, ADIBOT, is a UV-C disinfection robot platform that serves customers in regulated settings around the world. TGR team members come from diverse disciplines and backgrounds and share a hands-on approach to building robotics products.

**Job Description:**

The Implementation Specialist, Life Sciences brings ADIBOT autonomous UV-C disinfection robots into GMP environments and makes them part of how each site runs. A new robot in a classified area changes a validated state, so the job is as much about change control, qualification, and documentation as it is about operator training.

You will own each life sciences account on site from purchase order through its first 90 days. You will work with the customer's QA, Validation, Microbiology, Facilities, EHS, and Operations teams, and with TGR Customer Success, Technical Support, and Sales.

**Responsibilities:**

* Plan each deployment around the customer's contamination control strategy and change control process, so the robot enters the site as a documented, risk-assessed addition to its cleaning and disinfection program.
* Assess site readiness before delivery, including classified areas, airlocks, material transfer routes, doorways, charging, network access, and the rules for running cycles.
* Supply the technical package for the customer's change control: equipment description, UV-C safety data, and inputs to the risk assessment.
* Support the customer's QA team on site through IQ/OQ/PQ while they execute and approve the protocols.
* Become the subject matter expert on the robot and its disinfection protocols. Advise QA and Microbiology on available measurement options, such as dosimetry and cycle records, within TGR-approved claims, and supply robot cycle records for the validation package.
* Answer QA questions on how cycle records are generated, stored, and exported.
* Train and certify operators in UV-C safety, and help the customer write SOPs, work instructions, and training records.
* Review fleet data with each customer, resolve operational bottlenecks, and identify areas for expansion.
* Notify customers of firmware updates and support their change assessment before and after each update.
* Hand each account to Customer Success at day 90 with open items, training records, and a utilization baseline.
* Bring field learnings back to Product and Engineering.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, microbiology or biotechnology, or equivalent work experience.
* 2 to 4 years of field-based, customer-facing technical work, ideally in pharma, biotech, or medical device manufacturing.
* Working knowledge of gowning and work inside classified areas, plus ISO 14644, EU GMP Annex 1, and good documentation practice under GMP regulations.
* Experience with IQ/OQ/PQ and change control, whether you wrote, executed, or supported the protocols.
* Hands-on experience deploying or servicing complex machinery, and confidence troubleshooting hardware and software on site. Network troubleshooting experience is a plus.
* Familiarity with environmental monitoring and cleaning validation.
* Clear technical writing for SOPs, work instructions, and training records.
* Ability to travel 60%, including some weekends.

**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**The Role:**
-------------

US defense systems run on technical data that is often decades old: scanned paper, hand-marked prints, partial models, and drawings that were never turned into 3D models. A part that exists only on an old drawing is hard to source. That slows how fast the armed forces and our prime customers can sustain and rebuild the systems that use it. Hadrian turns that data into manufacturing-ready models and drawings, so customers can keep their systems running and Hadrian can make or procure the parts.

As a CAD Modeler, you build the 3D models and 2D drawings for naval and aerospace parts, starting from whatever the customer sends. You also build the models and drawings for each manufacturing state (M-state) of a part: the in-process configurations the factory builds and inventories on the way to the final part. Our engineers define each M-state, and you model, draw, and configure it. You own your parts from first model through release and every change after it.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build manufacturing-ready 3D models from naval prints, aerospace drawings, partial models, and other customer documents, matching the customer's definition feature for feature.
* Make the 2D drawings the factory runs on, from your models or the customer's.
* Build the models and drawings for each M-state of a part.
* Work out conflicting or unclear views against the rest of the drawing.
* Keep PLM data correct and structured, and send your parts through the release workflow.
* Carry each customer change through the customer geometry and every related M-state across the part family.
* Build models that tooling, programming, and inspection teams can use as a base.
* Work with manufacturing teams and turn around the model and drawing changes they need.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* 3+ years building production CAD models and drawings for hardware a factory made.
* Expert use of one parametric 3D CAD application, with models the next person can change. NX preferred; CATIA, Creo, or SolidWorks also fit.
* Experience building 3D models from complex 2D drawings with no existing model, including internal features that only show in a section view.
* Reads and drafts GD&T per ASME Y14.5, weld and NDT symbols per AWS A2.4, and drawings to ASME Y14.100.
* Experience releasing parts and controlling changes in a PLM system.
* Asks when a drawing cannot answer a question instead of guessing.
* Sets their own release schedule across many parts and switches priorities quickly.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Production work in Siemens NX.
* Experience with naval or shipyard drawings, customer data packages, and old or hand-drawn prints.
* Has modeled and drawn in-process (M-state) configurations that differ from the final customer definition.
* Has run a customer change process and an internal change process at the same time.
* Background in machined parts, welded assemblies, tooling, and CMM or scan inspection.
* Spots when one parametric model can cover a whole family of part numbers, and builds it that way.

We are seeking a Clinical Laboratory Coordinator to join our team in the Glendale, CA Early Phase Clinical Unit (EPCU). As a Laboratory Coordinator, you will play an essential role in supporting clinical trial studies through the coordination and execution of laboratory operations that help advance innovative treatments for patients. This position serves as a key laboratory resource, ensuring biological samples are processed, handled, documented, stored, and shipped in accordance with study protocols.

You will act as a laboratory study lead on assigned studies, collaborating with Clinical Research Coordinators, laboratory staff, sponsors, vendors, and cross functional teams to support high quality study delivery. **About the role**

The QC Technician is the last check between our electronics and the field. You will flash firmware onto circuit boards every day, run functional tests, and make sure every board that leaves the bench is correctly programmed, traceable, and working.

This is a hands-on, bench-based role on the hardware production team. You will work closely with hardware and firmware engineers, follow documented procedures, and flag anything that looks off before it reaches a vehicle.

* Use multimeters, power supplies, and basic test equipment to check voltages and continuity.

**ABOUT ADVANCED ENERGY**

Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE’s power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.

  

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

As a Quality Control Technician in the R&D pilot line, you will play a hands-on role in verifying and validating the quality of new product builds through inspection, auditing, and issue detection. Your focus will be on ensuring that early-stage builds meet internal and customer quality standards before scaling up production. Will interact closely with Quality Managers and NPI assembly teams to ensure risks are detected and addressed at the earliest phase. You will also assist in generating Product Quality Plan documentation that outlines quality requirements and inspection points throughout the product lifecycle.

  

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Perform in-process and final quality audits through visual, dimensional, and functional checks on prototypes and pilot units during NPI builds to verify conformance to assembly drawings, BOMs, and work instructions.
* Check work instructions, build travellers, and inspection records for accuracy and completion.
* Audit assembly processes for adherence to specifications, workmanship and IPC standards.
* Record, classify, and escalate quality issues in real time using the defined QMS tools.
* Work closely with engineers and technicians to identify root causes and validate corrections.
* Support First Article Inspections (FAI) and validate rework effectiveness.
* Monitor and track key NPI quality metrics like, FPY, and build conformance.
* Provide feedback on design or process issues encountered during audit and inspection.
* Assist in training build operators and technicians on quality criteria and defect awareness.
* Collaborate with NPI Quality Program Manager in generating Product Quality Plan documentation, including inspection checkpoints, quality control requirements, and critical-to-quality (CTQ) elements.
  

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

* This position is an in person role and based in the Redwood City, CA office.
* Environment: Office setting and engineering lab
  

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

Required:

* Able to read and interpret engineering drawings, BOMs, and assembly documentation.
* Basic understanding of defect categorization, rework tags, and NCR processes.
* Strong attention to details and ability to clearly communicate audit findings to both operators and engineers.
* Basic computer proficiency for data entry, documentation and reporting.
  

Preferred:

* Familiarity with QMS standards (ISO 9001), IPC-A-610 and R&D prototyping environments
* Prior experience in pilot lines, new product builds, or prototype audit environments
  

**EXPERIENCE:**

* 0 – 3 years of hands-on experience in quality inspection or NPI support role.
* Experience with hands-on inspection tools (e.g., calipers, microscopes, multimeters).
  

**EDUCATION:**

* Diploma or technical certification in Electronics, Mechanical, or Quality disciplines.

Actual compensation is influenced by an array of factors including, but not limited to, skill set, level of experience, and specific office location. The range of starting pay for this role is $24.00 per hour to $31.00 per hour.*

As part of our total rewards philosophy, we believe in offering and maintaining competitive compensation and benefits programs for our employees to attract and retain a talented, highly engaged workforce. Our compensation programs are focused on equitable, fair pay practices including market-based base pay, an annual pay-for-performance incentive plan for eligible positions, and a discounted Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
